title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of passenger cars powered by an internal combustion engine only, or powered by a hybrid electric power train with regard to the measurement of the emission of carbon dioxide and fuel consumption and/or the measurement of electric energy consumption and electric range, and of categories M1 and N1 vehicles powered by an electric power train only with regard to the measurement of electric energy consumption and electric range (CO2 emission/fuel consumption)
scope_summary: Approves vehicle types with regard to the measurement of CO2 emissions and fuel consumption and/or electric energy consumption and electric range, covering ICE-only, hybrid electric and pure electric power trains. It applies to M1 and N1 vehicles, except N1 vehicles whose engine type is approved under R49 when the manufacturer's worldwide annual N1 production is below 2,000 units.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to vehicles of categories M1 and N1 with regard to: (a) the measurement of the emission of carbon dioxide (CO2) and fuel consumption and/or to the measurement of electric energy consumption and electric range of vehicles powered by an internal combustion engine only or by a hybrid electric power train, (b) and to the measurement of electric energy consumption and electric range of vehicles powered by an electric power train only. It does not apply to a category N1 vehicle if both: (a) the engine type fitted to that type of vehicle has received type-approval pursuant to Regulation No. 49, and (b) the total annual worldwide production of N1 vehicles of the manufacturer is less than 2,000 units.
applies_to_components: periodically regenerating system (anti-pollution device, e.g. catalytic converter, particulate trap)
relation_to_other_regulations: N1 vehicles whose engine type is type-approved under UN Regulation No. 49 are excluded if the manufacturer's worldwide annual N1 production is below 2,000 units.
For M1 and N1 vehicles type-approved for emissions under UN Regulation No. 83, the technical service checks during the test that ICE or hybrid vehicles conform to the R83 limit values.
Vehicle categories as defined in Annex 7 to the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3).
Approval numbers currently indicate the 01 series of amendments.

defined_terms.definition: The approval of a vehicle type with regard to the measurement of energy consumption (fuel or electric energy).
A category of power driven vehicles which do not differ in essential respects such as body, power train, transmission, traction battery (if applicable), tyres and unladen mass.

Mass of the vehicle in running order without crew, passengers or load, but with full fuel tank, cooling liquid, service and traction batteries, oils, onboard/portable charger, tools and spare wheel as applicable.
The unladen mass of the vehicle increased by a uniform figure of 100 kg.
The technically permissible maximum mass declared by the manufacturer.
For pure electric vehicles, the reference mass for M1 vehicles and the unladen mass plus half the full load for N1 vehicles.
A motor vehicle of category N1 designed and constructed exclusively or principally for conveying goods.
A lorry with the cab integrated into the body.
A device which enriches the air/fuel mixture of the engine temporarily, to assist starting.
A device which assists engine starting without enrichment of the air/fuel mixture, e.g. glow plug, changed injection timing.
The system of energy storage device(s), energy converter(s) and transmission(s) that converts stored energy to mechanical energy delivered at the wheels for propulsion.
Vehicle powered by an internal combustion engine only.
A system of one or more electric energy storage devices, electric power conditioning devices and electric machines converting stored electric energy to mechanical energy at the wheels for propulsion.
Vehicle powered by an electric power train only.
A power train with at least two different energy converters and two different on-board energy storage systems for vehicle propulsion.
A power train that draws propulsion energy from both a consumable fuel and an on-vehicle electrical energy/power storage device (e.g. battery, capacitor, flywheel/generator).
Total distance covered during complete combined cycles until the energy from external charging of the battery (or other electric energy storage device) is depleted, measured per Annex 9.
A vehicle powered by a hybrid power train.
A vehicle, including those using fuel only to recharge the electrical storage device, that draws propulsion energy from both a consumable fuel and an electrical energy/power storage device.
For pure electric vehicles or OVC hybrids, the distance that can be driven electrically on one fully charged battery (or other storage device), measured per Annexes 7 and 9.
An anti-pollution device (e.g. catalytic converter, particulate trap) requiring a periodical regeneration process in less than 4,000 km of normal operation.
A flex fuel vehicle that can run on different mixtures of hydrogen and NG/biomethane.
A vehicle powered by a fuel cell converting chemical energy from hydrogen into electric energy for propulsion.

applicability_hints: This is a whole-vehicle approval (M1/N1); individual components are not approved under R101, but any power train component (engine, transmission, battery, electric machine, power controller, charger, tyres) is part of the vehicle type and a change may require extension (sections 6-7).
Tyres, body, transmission, traction battery and unladen mass are criteria defining the vehicle type, so changes to these may require a new approval or extension.
Anti-pollution devices like catalytic converters or particulate filters that regenerate within 4,000 km trigger the Annex 10 periodically regenerating system procedure.
Onboard and portable chargers are counted in unladen mass, affecting reference/test mass and thus inertia class.
Pure electric N1 and M1 vehicles fall under R101 for electric energy consumption and range even without fuel consumption.
Small-volume N1 manufacturers (<2,000/year worldwide) using R49-approved engines are excluded.
Hybrids are categorised by off-vehicle charging capability and presence of an operating mode switch, which determines the Annex 8 test procedure.
